eight: noun. NATO & ICAO radiotelephony clear code (spelling-alphabet name) for the digit 8.
eighteen: numeral. The cardinal number occurring after seventeen and before nineteen
eth: noun. A letter (capital Ð, small ð) introduced into Old English to represent its dental fricative, then not distinguished from the letter thorn, no longer used in English but still in modern use in Icelandic, the IPA and other phonetic alphabets to represent the voiced dental fricative "th" sound as in the English word th en.
ethene: noun. The organic chemical compound ethylene.
gee: interjection. A general exclamation of surprise or frustration.
gene: noun. A theoretical unit of heredity of living organisms which may take several values and (in principle) predetermines a precise trait of an organism's form (phenotype), such as hair color.
genet: noun. Any of several Old World nocturnal, carnivorous mammals, of the genus Genetta, most of which have a spotted coat and a long, ringed tail.
genie: noun. A jinn, a being descended from the jann, normally invisible to the human eye, but who may also appear in animal or human form.
ghee: noun. A type of clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.
gin: noun. A colourless non - aged alcoholic liquor made by distilling fermented grains such as barley, corn, oats or rye with juniper berries; the base for many cocktails.
git: noun. A silly, incompetent, stupid, or annoying person (usually a man).
hen: noun. A female chicken (Gallus gallus), especially a sexually mature one kept for her eggs.
hent: verb. To take hold of, to grasp.
hie: verb. To hasten; to go quickly, to hurry.
hin: noun. A former Hebrew liquid measure of volume (about 3.8 L).
hinge: noun. A jointed or flexible device that allows the pivoting of a door etc.
nee: interjection. no, used to express no as a quantity, i.e. not any, like German kein /Dutch geen /French rien.
neigh: noun. The cry of a horse.
net: noun. A mesh of string, cord or rope.
night: noun. The time when the Sun is below the horizon when the sky is dark.
nit: noun. The egg of a louse.
nth: adjective. Occurring at position n in a sequence.
tee: noun. The name of the Latin script letter T / t.
teeing: verb. present participle and gerund of tee
teen: noun. Synonym of teenager: a person between 13 and 19 years old (inclusive).
teg: noun. A sheep (originally a ewe) in its second year, or from the time it is weaned until it is first shorn.
ten: noun. NATO, ICAO, ITU & IMO radiotelephony code for 10, used only with o'clock to indicate direction.
the: article. Used before a noun phrase, including a simple noun The definite grammatical article that shows that the noun phrase that immediately follows it is definitely identifiable......because it has already been mentioned, is to be completely specified in the same sentence, or very shortly thereafter.
thee: pronoun. Objective and reflexive case of thou.
theine: noun. Caffeine when present in tea.
thin: adjective. Having little thickness or extent from one surface to its opposite.
thine: determiner. Second-person singular prevocalic possessive determiner (preconsonantal form: thy).
thing: noun. That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, object, quality or concept.
tin: noun. A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
tine: noun. A spike or point on an implement or tool, especially a prong of a fork or a tooth of a comb.
ting: interjection. Representing a high-pitched sharp sound like a small bell being struck.
tinge: noun. A small added amount of colour; a small added amount of some other thing.
ehing: verb. present participle and gerund of eh
ginete: noun. A trooper; a mounted soldier.
heng: noun. The character ꜧ, combining an h and an eng, which stands for the hypothetical phoneme in English that includes both [h] and [ŋ] as its allophones.
henge: noun. A prehistoric enclosure in the form of a circle or circular arc defined by a raised circular bank and a circular ditch usually running inside the bank, with one or more entrances leading into the enclosed open space.
ing: noun. A meadow, especially a low meadow near a river; water meadow.
neet: noun. Alternative letter-case form of NEET.
nete: noun. In Ancient Greek musical theory, the highest-pitched fixed note in the farther tetrachord on a lyre, always pitched a perfect fourth above the paramese, with two movable notes between them, the trite (lower in pitch) and the paranete (higher in pitch).
neti: noun. Nasal irrigation performed using a neti pot as part of Hatha yoga.
teenie: noun. A sixteenth of a dollar, a unit in which stocks could formerly be traded.
tehee: interjection. Alternative spelling of tee hee.
teheeing: verb. present participle and gerund of tehee
tenge: noun. The basic monetary unit of Kazakhstan; subdivided into tiyin.
theeing: verb. present participle and gerund of thee
thig: verb. To solicit or receive, usually by begging; ask as alms.
tig: verb. To touch lightly or playfully; to trifle, dally.
tige: noun. A steel pin in early rifles.
